key_features.classic_presentation: Biliary colic presents with EPISODIC (comes and goes) right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain that occurs 30 minutes to 2 hours AFTER EATING, especially after FATTY OR GREASY MEALS. Each episode lasts 30 minutes to 6 hours (shorter than cholecystitis which lasts >6 hours), then COMPLETELY RESOLVES between episodes. Pain is SEVERE (7-10/10), steady (not crampy), and may RADIATE TO RIGHT SHOULDER OR BACK. Pain is caused by gallstone temporarily blocking the cystic duct. Key associated symptoms: Nausea without vomiting (or minimal vomiting), bloating, belching. NO FEVER (fever suggests cholecystitis). Location: RUQ or epigastric pain. Pattern: RECURRENT episodes over weeks to months - patient usually has had similar episodes before. Key positives: Pain triggered by specific foods (fried foods, fatty meats, dairy), pain-free between attacks. Key negatives: CONSTANT pain that doesn't resolve suggests cholecystitis not colic. Fever rules out simple biliary colic. Jaundice suggests bile duct stone (choledocholithiasis).

red_flags: Pain lasting >6 hours with fever - suggests acute cholecystitis, needs urgent evaluation
Jaundice (yellow skin/eyes) - bile duct obstruction, needs urgent imaging and possible ERCP
Severe pain with vomiting and unable to tolerate liquids - dehydration risk
